SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a cardinal point? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North-west
   C. South-west
   D. North-east

2. Which direction is Nakuru from Nairobi? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. North-west
   C. East
   D. South-east

3. A county is divided into smaller parts called what? (1 mark)
   A. Countries
   B. Sub-counties
   C. Oceans
   D. Continents

4. Which county has a neighbouring county called Kiambu to its north? (1 mark)
   A. Turkana
   B. Kisumu
   C. Mombasa
   D. Nairobi

5. On a physical map, what colour is often used for high mountains? (1 mark)
   A. Brown
   B. Pink
   C. Blue
   D. White

6. What would you draw as a symbol for a river on a map? (1 mark)
   A. A green triangle
   B. A red square
   C. A black circle
   D. A wavy blue line

7. Which of these is a problem of the rainy season? (1 mark)
   A. Flooding and muddy roads
   B. Very dry grass
   C. Shortage of rain
   D. Thick dust

8. How can you keep safe from the sun in the hot season? (1 mark)
   A. Stay in the sun all day
   B. Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   C. Avoid drinking water
   D. Play in the hottest part of the day

9. Which symbol on a weather chart shows rain? (1 mark)
   A. A cloud with lines falling from it
   B. A thermometer
   C. A yellow sun
   D. A plain cloud

10. Which of these actions helps to conserve a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving litter
   B. Breaking off small pieces
   C. Climbing on old walls
   D. Reporting anyone who damages it

11. A tailor makes uniforms and a farmer buys them. What does the tailor need from the farmer? (1 mark)
   A. Food or money from selling food
   B. Nothing at all
   C. A tractor for sewing
   D. Cloth from the moon

12. What do traders do for farmers? (1 mark)
   A. Grow their crops
   B. Build their houses
   C. Buy their crops and take them to markets
   D. Teach their children

13. What do we call an area where many people live close together? (1 mark)
   A. Sparsely populated
   B. Wild
   C. Densely populated
   D. Empty

14. What does population distribution mean? (1 mark)
   A. How many trees are in an area
   B. How tall the mountains are
   C. How people are spread out in an area
   D. How much rain falls

15. Who can tell you about the history of your school? (1 mark)
   A. A stranger who has never visited
   B. The headteacher or teachers who have been there long
   C. A random person
   D. A shop

16. What is discipline? (1 mark)
   A. Running away
   B. Doing what you like
   C. Shouting
   D. Controlling yourself and following rules

17. Where might you see a school motto? (1 mark)
   A. On the badge or gate
   B. In a river
   C. In the sky
   D. On a rain cloud

18. What is a timeline? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of a school
   B. A weather chart
   C. A line showing events in the order they happened
   D. A kind of ruler

19. Where is titanium mined in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Nakuru
   C. Nyeri
   D. Kwale

20. Which of these is a human resource? (1 mark)
   A. A skilled farmer
   B. A mineral
   C. A forest
   D. A lake

21. In Figure 3 of the lesson, the sugar factory employs 7 hundred workers. How many workers is that? (1 mark)
   A. 70
   B. 7
   C. 700
   D. 7,000

22. What should you do when visiting a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Stay with the group and not touch machines
   B. Run around
   C. Shout
   D. Touch all machines

23. What should be done with profit from a school project? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it away
   B. Hide it
   C. Share it secretly
   D. Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books

24. In school life, what is a right? (1 mark)
   A. A rule to break
   B. A duty you refuse
   C. A punishment
   D. Something you are allowed to have or do

25. What is a citizen? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of law
   B. A type of school
   C. A visitor who never returns
   D. A member of a country or community with rights and duties

26. If you see a pupil being bullied, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Join in
   C. Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   D. Ignore

27. Which law forbids child labour and FGM in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Only a poster
   B. The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act
   C. Only school rules
   D. Nothing forbids it

28. How are members of the Children's Government chosen? (1 mark)
   A. By buying votes
   B. By election
   C. By force
   D. By luck at a market

29. Which quality is important for a pupil leader? (1 mark)
   A. Honesty
   B. Selfishness
   C. Laziness
   D. Bullying

30. How many county governments are there in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 47
   B. 57
   C. 37
   D. 27

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how you would prepare a poster on the school values. (4 marks)

32. Explain why the county assembly must check the work of the governor. (5 marks)

33. A bar graph shows sub-county A has 40 thousand people and sub-county B has 25 thousand. Find the total population of the two sub-counties. (3 marks)

34. Explain how the Tana River helps people in Kenya. (3 marks)

35. Explain what peace means in a school. (2 marks)

36. Describe what people do in the cold season to stay healthy and warm. (4 marks)

37. Explain what a Children's Government is. (2 marks)

38. Describe five actions that show good citizenship in school. (5 marks)

39. Name the four seasons in the county. (2 marks)

40. Describe how you would prepare for a class visit to a museum, and what you would do during the visit. (5 marks)

41. Design a poster: write a slogan and list three qualities of a good leader you would show on it. (5 marks)

42. Explain the meaning of democracy. (2 marks)

43. Explain why many factories are built near big towns. (3 marks)

44. Name three kinds of community leaders. (3 marks)

45. Give two examples of natural resources. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — West
   Only north, east, south and west are cardinal points. The others are in-between points.

2. B — North-west
   Nakuru is north-west of Nairobi.

3. B — Sub-counties
   Counties are divided into sub-counties, and sub-counties into wards.

4. D — Nairobi
   Kiambu lies to the north of Nairobi County.

5. A — Brown
   Brown shows high land such as mountains.

6. D — A wavy blue line
   Rivers are shown as wavy blue lines.

7. A — Flooding and muddy roads
   Heavy rain can flood rivers and make roads muddy.

8. B — Wear a hat, drink water and rest in the shade
   These habits protect us from heat.

9. A — A cloud with lines falling from it
   Falling lines under a cloud show rain.

10. D — Reporting anyone who damages it
   Reporting damage helps protect the place.

11. A — Food or money from selling food
   The tailor depends on the farmer for food.

12. C — Buy their crops and take them to markets
   Traders buy from farmers and sell in towns.

13. C — Densely populated
   Dense means crowded.

14. C — How people are spread out in an area
   Distribution is about where people live.

15. B — The headteacher or teachers who have been there long
   Reliable people and records give true information.

16. D — Controlling yourself and following rules
   Discipline is self-control and obeying rules.

17. A — On the badge or gate
   Mottos are often on badges and gates.

18. C — A line showing events in the order they happened
   A timeline shows events in order.

19. D — Kwale
   Titanium is mined in Kwale County.

20. A — A skilled farmer
   People's skills and labour are human resources.

21. C — 700
   7 hundreds = 700.

22. A — Stay with the group and not touch machines
   Safety rules protect visitors.

23. D — Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books
   Profit should be used openly and wisely.

24. D — Something you are allowed to have or do
   Rights are things we are allowed, such as learning.

25. D — A member of a country or community with rights and duties
   Citizens belong to a community and have rights and duties.

26. C — Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   Reporting helps to stop bullying.

27. B — The law of Kenya, including the Constitution and the Children Act
   Kenyan law protects children.

28. B — By election
   Pupils vote for their leaders.

29. A — Honesty
   Leaders must be honest and fair.

30. A — 47
   There are 47 counties, each with its own government.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the values, write a large title, draw a picture for each value, and use bright colours that can be seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: To make sure county money is used honestly, to prevent misuse of power, to make sure services reach people, to protect citizens' interests, and to keep the governor accountable.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 65 thousand, which is 65,000 people.
   Working / marking points: 40 + 25 = 65 thousand. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 65 thousand, 1 mark for 65,000.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It supplies water, its dams produce electric power, and its water is used for irrigation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Peace means pupils and teachers live together safely, respect each other and settle disagreements without fighting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for safety and respect, 1 mark for solving conflict peacefully.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: They wear warm clothes, eat and drink hot foods, sleep under blankets, and wash their hands to avoid colds and flu.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a group of pupils elected by their classmates to help run the school and speak for pupils, guided by a teacher.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for elected pupils, 1 mark for helping and speaking for pupils.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Arrive on time, keep the compound clean, respect teachers, share with others, and report bullying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each action.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Hot, cold, dry and rainy.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for all four, 1 mark for two or three.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission from the teacher and the museum, prepare questions, take a notebook, stay with the group, listen to the guide, take notes and do not touch objects.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 5.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: A slogan such as A Good Leader Serves, and qualities such as honest, fair and kind, with a picture.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a slogan, 3 marks for three qualities, 1 mark for a picture.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Democracy is rule by the people, where everyone has a say in choosing leaders and making decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rule by the people, 1 mark for having a say.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Many customers live there. Workers live nearby. Roads and other services are available.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Religious leaders, clan elders and village elders. Accept chiefs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each kind.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water and soil. Accept forests, minerals, wildlife or fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.
